questions.prompt: In 2 to 5 sentences, explain how Swift actors protect mutable state against data races. Why must external callers use the await keyword?

rubric.criterion: Explains that actors enforce mutual exclusion allowing only one task access at a time
Explains that external callers must use await because the calling task may need to suspend
Mentions that internal access to state inside actor methods is synchronous

questions.modelAnswer: Swift actors protect mutable state by enforcing mutual exclusion so only one task can execute on an instance at any moment. External callers must write await because their task might need to suspend while waiting for another task to finish with the actor. Inside the actor's own methods, state access is direct and synchronous.

questions.prompt: In 2 to 5 sentences, explain actor reentrancy in Swift. Describe a potential bug that can happen across an await suspension point inside an actor.

rubric.criterion: Explains that an actor releases its lock when a method suspends at an await point
Explains that other tasks can execute and mutate actor state while the first task is suspended
Describes bugs where assumed state before await is invalidated upon resumption

questions.modelAnswer: Actor reentrancy means an actor releases its execution lock whenever an internal method reaches an await suspension point. While suspended, other tasks can execute on that actor and mutate its properties. A bug occurs if a method assumes state remains unchanged across the await, such as duplicate item purchases when balances drop during suspension.

questions.prompt: In 2 to 5 sentences, explain the purpose of the nonisolated keyword on an actor. What rules govern which properties a nonisolated method can read?

rubric.criterion: Explains that nonisolated allows members to be called synchronously from outside without await
Explains that nonisolated members can only access immutable let constants or other nonisolated APIs
Mentions protocol conformances like CustomStringConvertible or Hashable as common use cases

questions.modelAnswer: The nonisolated keyword allows an actor member to be called synchronously from the outside without writing await. Because it runs outside actor isolation, a nonisolated method can only read immutable let constants or call other nonisolated code. This is commonly used to conform actors to synchronous protocols like CustomStringConvertible or Hashable.

questions.prompt: In 2 to 5 sentences, explain what @MainActor does. Why is it standard practice to annotate SwiftUI view models with @MainActor?

rubric.criterion: Explains that @MainActor is a global actor binding code execution to the main thread
Explains that UI frameworks require state updates on the main thread to prevent crashes
Mentions avoiding manual DispatchQueue.main.async dispatch boilerplate

questions.modelAnswer: @MainActor is a global actor that ensures all isolated properties and functions execute on the main thread. Annotating view models with @MainActor guarantees that published UI state mutations always occur on the main thread without manual dispatch calls. This prevents background thread UI violation crashes and rendering glitches.

questions.prompt: In 2 to 5 sentences, explain how an image caching actor can avoid duplicate in-flight network requests caused by actor reentrancy.
questions.lessonSection: How to answer in the interview

rubric.criterion: Explains storing in-flight Task handles inside a cache dictionary before awaiting the network
Explains that subsequent callers await the existing in-flight task rather than starting a duplicate
Mentions replacing the task with the completed image result upon download completion

questions.modelAnswer: To prevent duplicate network downloads during actor reentrancy, an image cache actor can store in-flight Task handles in a dictionary. When a request arrives, the actor checks if a task is already running for that URL. Subsequent requests await the existing task value rather than spawning a duplicate network request.
